column7: 2026-11-05: 1024KB bug in bytes.format: unit is chosen from raw magnitude, then toFixed rounds up to 1024 (bytes 1048571-1048575 at default 2 decimals; same at MB/GB/TB boundaries, negatives, lower decimalPlaces). Fix direction is truncation (floor toward zero at decimalPlaces), per finance rule. NO code changed yet: user said to leave code alone until finance signs off the page wording.

2026-11-05: Open design points (my suggestions, not decided by user): truncate toward zero incl. negatives; avoid float error in Math.floor(val*100)/100; consider opt-in option (e.g. rounding:'floor') vs changing default since format is used beyond billing; update History.md/Readme. Waiting on finance sign-off before implementing.

2026-11-05: capacity-alerts: ops want bytes.format to round UP (never show less than real usage) at the shown precision: 1048575->1MB, 1025->1.01KB, 2047->2KB. This is the opposite of billing-ui's truncate rule (finance), so it must NOT change the default behaviour; plan is an opt-in option. User said describe only, no code changes yet (ops still reviewing alert thresholds). My choices, not user's: option name, ceil on magnitude for negatives, integer-based math.

2026-11-05: bytes.format now truncates toward zero (never rounds up) by default, per finance rule; implemented in truncate() in index.js after finance sign-off. Strips float noise via toPrecision(15) first so 1.2*mb -> 1.2MB. Existing round-up tests changed. BigInt used only for values >=1e21.
